content: [{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) - A Technical Tutorial"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) is a service that lets you easily provision, manage, and deploy Secure Sockets Layer/Transport Layer Security (SSL/TLS) certificates for use with AWS services and your internal connected resources. SSL/TLS certificates are used to establish secure network connections and protect the integrity and confidentiality of data transferred between servers and clients. ACM removes the time-consuming manual process of purchasing, uploading, and renewing SSL/TLS certificates."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Key Features of AWS Certificate Manager"},{"order":4,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Simplified Certificate Management: ACM handles the complexity of creating, installing, and renewing SSL/TLS certificates."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Free SSL/TLS Certificates: ACM provides SSL/TLS certificates for use with ACM-integrated services, such as Elastic Load Balancing, Amazon CloudFront, and Amazon API Gateway, at no charge."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Automatic Renewal: ACM automatically renews SSL/TLS certificates that are used with ACM-integrated services, reducing the risk of downtime due to expired certificates."},{"order":7,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Private Certificates: ACM allows you to create and manage private certificates for internal resources."},{"order":8,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Import Certificates: You can import SSL/TLS certificates from third-party certificate authorities into ACM."},{"order":9,"type":"subheading","text":"How ACM Works"},{"order":10,"type":"paragraph","text":"ACM integrates with other AWS services to simplify the process of securing your applications. Here's a general overview of how it works:"},{"order":11,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Request a Certificate: You can request a public or private SSL/TLS certificate from ACM through the AWS Management Console, AWS CLI, or AWS SDKs."},{"order":12,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Validate Domain Ownership: For public certificates, ACM requires you to validate that you own or control the domain names listed in the certificate request. This can be done through email validation or DNS validation."},{"order":13,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Deploy the Certificate: Once the certificate is issued, you can deploy it to ACM-integrated services, such as Elastic Load Balancing, CloudFront, or API Gateway. ACM automatically distributes the certificate to these services."},{"order":14,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Automatic Renewal: ACM automatically renews the certificate before it expires, ensuring that your applications remain secure."},{"order":15,"type":"subheading","text":"Requesting a Certificate using the AWS CLI"},{"order":16,"type":"paragraph","text":"To request a certificate using the AWS CLI, you can use the 'request-certificate' command. Here's an example:"},{"order":17,"type":"code","text":"aws acm request-certificate --domain-name example.com --subject-alternative-names www.example.com --validation-method DNS"},{"order":18,"type":"paragraph","text":"This command requests a certificate for 'example.com' with 'www.example.com' as a subject alternative name. The validation method is set to DNS, which requires you to create a CNAME record in your DNS configuration."},{"order":19,"type":"subheading","text":"Validating Domain Ownership"},{"order":20,"type":"paragraph","text":"ACM provides two methods for validating domain ownership:"},{"order":21,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Email Validation: ACM sends an email to the registered contacts for the domain name, who must approve the certificate request."},{"order":22,"type":"bullet_point","text":"DNS Validation: ACM provides a CNAME record that you must add to your DNS configuration. ACM checks for the presence of this record to validate domain ownership. DNS validation is recommended as it allows for automatic renewal."},{"order":23,"type":"subheading","text":"Deploying a Certificate to Elastic Load Balancing (ELB)"},{"order":24,"type":"paragraph","text":"To deploy an ACM certificate to an Elastic Load Balancer, follow these steps:"},{"order":25,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Create or update your load balancer listener to use HTTPS (port 443)."},{"order":26,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Select the ACM certificate from the list of available certificates."},{"order":27,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Save the changes to your load balancer configuration."},{"order":28,"type":"paragraph","text":"The ELB will now use the ACM certificate to encrypt traffic between clients and your backend servers."},{"order":29,"type":"subheading","text":"Importing Certificates"},{"order":30,"type":"paragraph","text":"If you already have an SSL/TLS certificate from a third-party certificate authority, you can import it into ACM. You'll need the certificate body, the private key, and the certificate chain (if applicable). Use the following AWS CLI command:"},{"order":31,"type":"code","text":"aws acm import-certificate --certificate file://certificate.pem --private-key file://private-key.pem --certificate-chain file://chain.pem"},{"order":32,"type":"paragraph","text":"Replace 'certificate.pem', 'private-key.pem', and 'chain.pem' with the actual paths to your certificate files."},{"order":33,"type":"subheading","text":"Private Certificates"},{"order":34,"type":"paragraph","text":"ACM also allows you to create private certificates for use within your internal network. These certificates are not trusted by public browsers, but they can be used to secure communication between your internal resources. To create a private certificate authority (CA), use the 'create-certificate-authority' command:"},{"order":35,"type":"code","text":"aws acm create-certificate-authority --certificate-authority-configuration '{\"KeyAlgorithm\":\"RSA_2048\", \"SigningAlgorithm\":\"SHA256WITHRSA\", \"Subject\":{\"CommonName\":\"MyInternalCA\"}}' --certificate-authority-type ROOT --revocation-configuration '{\"CrlConfiguration\":{\"Enabled\":false}}' --idempotency-token myuniquetoken"},{"order":36,"type":"paragraph","text":"After creating the CA, you can issue private certificates using the 'issue-certificate' command."},{"order":37,"type":"subheading","text":"Best Practices"},{"order":38,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Use DNS validation for automatic certificate renewal."},{"order":39,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Regularly monitor your certificates for expiration."},{"order":40,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Use ACM-integrated services to simplify certificate deployment and management."},{"order":41,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Implement proper access control policies to protect your ACM resources."},{"order":42,"type":"subheading","text":"Troubleshooting"},{"order":43,"type":"paragraph","text":"If you encounter issues with ACM, consider the following:"},{"order":44,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Verify that your domain validation records are correctly configured."},{"order":45,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Check the ACM event logs for any errors or warnings."},{"order":46,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Ensure that your IAM roles have the necessary permissions to access ACM resources."},{"order":47,"type":"paragraph","text":"By following these guidelines, you can effectively use AWS Certificate Manager to secure your applications and services."}]
